question.problem:
Consider the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}+4y=f(x),\,y(1)=-3
$$

where $f(x)$ is a $3$-periodic function. Fill in the missing part in the solution of the IVP, where the infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution ${y}_{p}$ of the differential equation.

*Hint: In this specific problem, the forcing function $f(x)$ is chosen such that the particular solution ${y}_{p}$ satisfies ${y}_{p}(1)=0.$*

The solution is 

$y(x)∼$   
{{field-1}} 
$+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}cos\,(\frac{2\pi n}{3}x)+{b}_{n}sin\,(\frac{2\pi n}{3}x))$
